Load it with ToolSearch (select:Artifact) before writing any document, plan, analysis or visual, and whenever other people come up as readers, even after the work is written. Its description says whether to publish, offer a page or do neither. What follows applies whether or not it is loaded yet. Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL. When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A write-up that will be posted in a channel or a thread is still published, so the post can carry the link; when it is short, Claude also gives the text in its reply, ready to paste. When it might be passed along but nothing says so, Claude offers the page in one line instead of saying nothing. When the person asks for the file itself, such as "just give me the .html file" or "save these notes as a .md file", Claude gives them that file and does not publish it.

- animation-vocabulary: Reverse-lookup glossary that turns a vague description of a web animation or motion effect into its exact term ("the bouncy thing when a popover opens" → Pop in; "the iOS rubber-band scroll" → Rubber-banding). Use when the user asks "what's it called when…", or describes a motion effect without knowing its name and wants the right word to prompt an AI or designer with. For naming an effect, not designing or building one.
- apple-design: Apple's approach to interface design and fluid, physical motion, translated for the web. Use when building or reviewing gesture-driven UI, spring animations, drag/swipe/sheet interactions, momentum and interruptible transitions, translucent materials and depth, typography (optical sizing, tracking, leading), reduced-motion, or the design foundations (feedback, spatial consistency, restraint) behind Apple-style interfaces.
- emil-design-eng: This skill encodes Emil Kowalski's philosophy on UI polish, component design, animation decisions, and the invisible details that make software feel great.
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- self-code-review: Deep, evidence-based self review of the current branch against its base. Use when the user asks to "self review", "review my branch", "review my PR", "review my code", "review my changes", or wants a thorough pre-push critique.

  works. Never trade a working product for unfinished complexity.

  complexity or improve reliability. Do not reimplement common
  functionality without a clear reason.
- Lean on the dependencies already in the project before writing your own
  implementation or adding packages. Do not assume a library lacks a
  capability without checking its documentation and types.
- Make architectural decisions for the long term. Do not accept a stopgap
  that only works for now and is meant to be replaced later.
- No em-dashes in prose or user-facing copy.
- Terse by default: after an action, state what changed in three lines or
  fewer. Explain only when asked.
- Surface non-trivial design decisions before baking them into a plan or an
  implementation.

Steffen Grabert, steffen.grabert@tum.de

TUM student. Python for data, ML and finance; TypeScript for web and
desktop. Recurring domains: investing and portfolio modelling, football
analytics, study tools.

# AGENTS.md

Rules for AI coding agents in this repo. Humans follow them too.

Hackathon repo, EHL Grand Finale, Munich, 10 to 11 Oct 2026. Code freeze and Live Final Sunday
12:00. Working agent first, polish second.

## Rules

- Do not preserve backward compatibility. Remove obsolete paths instead of adding layers,
  fallbacks or migrations.
- Choose the simplest implementation that fully meets the current requirement. No speculative
  abstractions, configuration or indirection.
- Grow in layers on a product that already works. Never trade a working agent for unfinished
  complexity.
- Keep components modular and concerns separated.
- Read `arena_kit` (in `.venv`) before writing a helper: cost function, quote parsing, data lookup
  and runners exist. We wrap the kit, never patch it. Guide:
  https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit/tree/main/starter-kit
- Never commit secrets. Keys live in `.env`. Never print, log or paste the arena key anywhere.
- All changes go through a PR against `main`, reviewed by one teammate. Branch `<firstname>/<topic>`.
  Agents may commit, push their branch and `gh pr create`; never push to `main`, force-push or merge.
- Run `uv run pytest -q && uv run ruff check .` before every PR.
- No em-dashes in prose or copy. Be terse: after an action, state what changed in three lines.

## The challenge

We are the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke. Our agent negotiates by e-mail with Tacto's
supplier bots (LLM personas with hidden economics) and closes one term sheet per case, or walks.

- **Score** per case: `(C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)`, clipped to 0..1. C is total cost
  over the horizon (price, uncovered need, payment, freight, lead time, quality, tooling, index
  clause, relationship charge), computed exactly by `arena_kit.total_cost`. No deal scores the
  alternative (0 if none). A broken must-have scores 0.
- **Live Final**: five waves of hidden cases, 8 minutes each, a wave's cases in parallel. Wave
  score = mean case score x 100; total = sum. New suppliers; up to a third mix supplier and case
  types practice never shows; some cite the Sunday 08:00 data release.

**Hard rules, breaking one can disqualify us:**
- No human in the loop during the final. The runner starts before 12:00 and is left alone.
- Agent code never calls `/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`,
  `/leaderboard`, `/v1/leaderboard`, `/results`, `/v1/results`.
- One key per team. No attacks on the arena or other teams (prompt-injecting bots counts).
- The final runs the commit we submit at 12:00. No pushes after that.

**Hard limits:**
- 60 s per message per thread from the supplier's reply; three timeouts in a row end the thread.
- 10 messages per thread, up to 3 term sheets per message, every sheet carries every `negotiable`
  field.
- Max 3 claim checks per message, one per sentence, ID and figure in the same sentence. A wrong
  figure or unknown ID is `contradicted` and costs trust.
- 10 calls/s and 10 open sessions per key.
- **Practice quota: 200 sessions per rolling 24 h for the whole team.** Sandbox (`case:D01`,
  `case:D02`) and the local simulator are free.

## Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `docs/learnings.md` | **read first**: what we know about the arena, suppliers and data, with evidence |
| `docs/design.md` | the agent we are building: modules, data, policy, build order |
| `docs/challenge.md`, `api.md`, `submission.md` | Tacto's brief, API and cost formula, hand-in (upstream copies) |
| `buyer/policy.py`, `runner.py` | the price engine: per-thread policy and the loop that plays a case (`docs/design.md`, Implemented) |
| `buyer/economics.py`, `claims.py`, `personas.py`, `writer.py`, `llm.py` | C and term planning, claim bank, persona signals, e-mail and model paragraph |
| `buyer/cli.py` | `buyer play`, `buyer run`, `buyer pull` |
| `tests/` | end to end against `arena-sim`, no network, no model |
| `exports/` | Saturday probe sessions as CSV/JSONL; schema in `exports/README.md` |
| `analysis/explore.py` | data package exploration: profiles, persona signals, report page |
| `data/package/` | the data package (gitignored); Sunday also `data/release-sunday/` |
| `logs/sessions/<set>/` | finished sessions with trace and back office (gitignored; Saturday's committed with `-f`) |
| `logs/runs/`, `logs/practice-v*.log` | our decisions per move (anchor, terms, claims, prices) and the practice run logs |

The MCP server `arena-data` (`.mcp.json`) gives SQL, ID lookup and documents over the package.

## Commands

```sh
uv sync                                         # install (Python 3.12)
uv run arena data                               # data package into data/
uv run arena me                                 # key works? quota left?
uv run buyer play case:D01 -v                   # sandbox: free
uv run buyer play case:P01 -v                   # practice: costs 1 of the team's 200
uv run buyer run --set practice --parallel 10   # all hosted practice cases: costs 10
uv run buyer pull --set practice                # finished sessions -> logs/sessions/
uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package   # local API, scripted supplier
uv run --with pandas python analysis/explore.py # data package -> analysis/out/
```

`--agent naive` plays the kit's baseline instead of ours.

## Working on the negotiation agent

- **Code owns numbers, the model owns words.** Every binding value (sheet, accept, walk away) is
  computed or checked in code with `total_cost` and `must_haves_ok`; every figure in an e-mail
  comes from code next to its data ID.
- **Never accept** a sheet that breaks a must-have or costs more than the alternative. Price
  unstated fields at the supplier's standard terms (`arena_kit.docs.standard_terms`).
- **Read the supplier.** What moves it is in the data (call notes, letters, news, quote remarks,
  payment history, scorecards). Trade what is cheap for us for what it values.
- **Score every lever per case.** The same term helps in one case and hurts in the next
  (coverage, payment days, start date, index clause, contract length).
- **Generalise.** No logic keyed on case or supplier IDs; runtime knowledge from the data package
  is fine if it works for unseen suppliers.
- **Don't leak** urgency, budget, a missing alternative or the target price.
- **Every model call has a hard timeout** well under 60 s, and the move still goes out if it
  fails. Measure latency per move.

## The learning loop

1. Try on the simulator or sandbox first. Spend practice quota only on a change you expect to
   help; check `uv run arena me` before batch runs.
2. After practice: `uv run buyer pull`, read `logs/sessions/` (trace, back office, cost breakdown).
3. Find why C_deal missed C_best, change the agent, score candidate sheets offline, play again.
4. Record each finding in `docs/learnings.md` in the same PR: date, tag (`arena` / `data` /
   `rules`), finding, evidence (session, case or data ID), consequence for the agent. Untested
   ideas go under Hypotheses; correct or delete entries that turn out wrong. Design changes go
   into `docs/design.md`. No new doc files without a reason.

## Sunday

- 08:00: `uv run arena data` again; the release lands in `data/release-sunday/`.
- 09:00: pre-flight, one practice case through the final machine and setup.
- 11:30: checklist in `docs/submission.md` (key, data, LLM credits, power, no sleep, log file).
- Before 12:00, from `main`: `uv run buyer run --set final --parallel 10 -v 2>&1 | tee logs/final.log`,
  then submit that commit hash on ehl.gg.

- [Research scope: own commits only](research-scope-own-commits.md): consolidating "my research" means Steffen's commits and sessions, not teammates' branches
- [Shared working tree](shared-working-tree.md) — peer sessions commit in the same checkout; re-check git state, never leave temporary constant edits
- [Elicit worktree](elicit-worktree.md) — experiments live in ../ehlcodacabana-elicit on branch steffen/elicit (PR #14), not in the shared checkout

{"add":195,"author":"Zuff2004","base":"main","body":"Supplier alternatives could be ignored because their index clause was excluded, or evaluated as a hybrid of quoted and retained terms. This change compares complete quoted packages against the current plan at supplier-equivalent value, chooses once, and preserves the exact evaluated package when mirroring. For example, an observed higher-price deadband alternative cost EUR 853.99 less in total than the standing quote.

It also refreshes active relationship targets after new terms/signals, answers fixed-payment requests without relying on the model, and removes unsupported payment-reliability and forecast-growth assertions. Mirrored packages must satisfy allowed options, fixed terms, must-haves and the alternative-cost gate. Explicit allowed `None` clauses remain valid regardless of option order.

No new case/supplier-specific rules, score targets, anchors or patience tuning. The former special index-concession path is removed: a price cut alone no longer justifies worse package terms. Supplier-equivalent valuation remains an estimate. Current main's clause-trading and claim changes are preserved.

Validation against main `3c02621`:

- `PYTHONPATH=. uv run --no-sync pytest -q`: 42 passed; `uv run --no-sync ruff check .`: passed, using the existing environment.
- Official local simulator, 24 case definitions × 12 scenarios × 2 data modes: 576 paired runs, 8 better / 568 equal / 0 worse; mean 0.661334 → 0.662484. Improvements are concentrated in P01 variants.
- Another 48 pairs with renamed case IDs: unchanged decisions. This is not supplier-ID invariance or an independent hosted holdout.
- Both variants: 409 matrix deals, zero exceptions, zero invalid accepted deals, zero deals worse than the alternative.
- Both retain 52 preexisting invalid-proposal stress runs: 48 impossible must-haves and four payment-floor variants. Those proposal-generation defects are outside this change and remain open.
- Zero hosted sessions and zero model calls. No claim of improved online score or proven absence of overfitting. Targeted regressions cover complete packages, option order, costlier counter concessions, exact mirroring and model-free fixed-payment answers.

`docs/learnings.md` records the evidence and rejected candidate: generalizing the old index-concession exception to all counters regressed 225/576 simulations, so that rule is absent from this PR. Local reproducibility artifacts are `/private/tmp/general-offer-pr-evidence/` in the evaluation workspace; raw synthetic logs are not committed.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

 ## Takeaways for the agent
 
 1. **Stay below the supplier's counter until the end; it agrees the moment our sheet reaches the
"""Numbers only: C of a sheet, what a sheet is worth to the supplier, the non-price terms we ask for
and, in relationship goals, the price below which a lower price costs us more than it saves.
Nothing here calls a model; every figure that reaches a term sheet comes from here."""

import itertools
import math

from arena_kit.cost import closing_terms, complete_offer, must_haves_ok, supplier_value, total_cost

RELATIONSHIP_GOALS = {"stabilise", "secure_supply"}


def cost(case, terms, std=None, est=None):
    """C in EUR; infinite for sheets the cost function cannot price. The relationship charge
    needs a full-cost estimate; without one it counts as 0."""
    if est is not None and not est.get("full_cost"):
        est = None
    try:
        return total_cost(case, terms, std, est)
    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError, ZeroDivisionError):
        return math.inf


def c_alt(case):
    alt = case["buyer"].get("alternative") or {}
    terms = alt.get("terms") or {}
    if alt.get("kind") in (None, "none") or not terms.get("unit_price"):
        return math.inf
    return cost(case, terms)


def deal_cost(case, terms, std, est=None):
    """The accept gate: C of a sheet with a price that keeps every must-have and is cheaper than
    the alternative (relationship charge included), else None. The C returned is the C checked."""
    if not terms.get("unit_price") or not must_haves_ok(case, terms, std):
        return None
    c = cost(case, terms, std, est)
    return c if c < c_alt(case) else None


def quoted_offer(case, terms, std=None):
    """An outgoing sheet with exactly the quoted effective package, never snapped terms."""
    effective = closing_terms(case, terms, std)
    if any(effective.get(k) != v for k, v in case.get("fixed_terms", {}).items()):
        return None
    offer = {k: effective.get(k) for k in case["negotiable"]}
    price = offer.get("unit_price")
    if not isinstance(price, (int, float)) or not math.isfinite(price) or price <= 0:
        return None
    opts = case.get("term_options", {})
    if any(opts.get(k) and v not in opts[k] for k, v in offer.items()):
        return None
    if closing_terms(case, offer, std) != effective:
        return None
    return offer if must_haves_ok(case, offer, std) else None


def known_incoterm(case, terms):
    """`terms` with an Incoterm the case prices; an unknown one (a hidden case's quote) would be a
    KeyError in the kit, so it falls back to the costliest, as `closing_terms` does for a gap."""
    freight = case["buyer"]["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    if terms.get("incoterm") in freight or "incoterm" not in terms:
        return terms
    return {**terms, "incoterm": max(freight, key=freight.get)}


def estimate(case, std, rate, full_cost=None, ppm=None, lead=None, overtime=0.0):
    """Our view of the supplier for `supplier_value` and the relationship term. `lead`: the lead
    time it quoted; `overtime`: what each day faster costs it, as a share of the price."""
    standard = known_incoterm(case, closing_terms(case, {}, known_incoterm(case, std or {})))
    est = {"standard": standard, "interest_rate": rate, "lead": lead, "overtime": overtime}
    if ppm is not None:
        est["ppm"] = ppm
    if full_cost:
        est["full_cost"] = full_cost
    est["index_moves"] = {}  # series -> its change over the last 12 months (share), what the supplier expects on
    return est


def clause_value(case, terms, est):
    """What an index clause is worth to the supplier per unit: it expects its driver to move on as
    it did over the last twelve months (what it cites in its quote), and the clause pays it that
    share beyond the deadband. Nordmark agreed at once to a copper clause 4 % below its fixed
    price (P02); the distributors priced the AS-14404 deadband at exactly this (P08, P18)."""
    clause = terms.get("index_clause")
    if not clause:
        return 0.0
    move = est.get("index_moves", {}).get(clause.get("series"))
    if move is None:
        return 0.0
    exposed = max(0.0, move - (clause.get("deadband_pct") or 0) / 100)
    return (clause.get("material_share") or 0) * exposed * (terms.get("unit_price") or 0)


def clause_cost_share(case, clause):
    """Our cost of a clause as a share of the spend: the case's path beyond the deadband plus the
    index risk charge."""
    b = case["buyer"]
    share, deadband = clause.get("material_share") or 0, (clause.get("deadband_pct") or 0) / 100
    path = abs(b.get("index_paths", {}).get(clause.get("series"), 0.0))
    return share * max(0.0, path - deadband) + share * b.get("index_risk_pct", 0) / 100


def clause_trade(case, est, min_gain=0.02):
    """The index clause worth trading: the supplier's value less our cost, as a share of the price,
    above `min_gain`; among equal gains the widest deadband (least risk). None when no clause pays
    (P08, P18: the supplier's value equals our cost) or the case has none to offer."""
    best = None
    for clause in case.get("term_options", {}).get("index_clause") or []:
        if not clause:
            continue
        move = est.get("index_moves", {}).get(clause.get("series"))
        if move is None:
            continue
        theirs = (clause.get("material_share") or 0) * max(0.0, move - (clause.get("deadband_pct") or 0) / 100)
        gain = theirs - clause_cost_share(case, clause)
        key = (round(gain, 4), clause.get("deadband_pct") or 0)
        if gain >= min_gain and (best is None or key > best[0]):
            best = (key, clause)
    return best[1] if best else None


def value(case, terms, est):
    """What a sheet is worth to the supplier per unit, in cash at its standard terms, less the
    overtime a faster delivery than it quoted costs it (fully booked suppliers: about 0.5 % of
    the price per day, P05 and P10)."""
    v = supplier_value(case, known_incoterm(case, terms), est) + clause_value(case, terms, est)
    lead, quoted = terms.get("lead_time_days"), est.get("lead")
    if est.get("overtime") and lead is not None and quoted and lead < quoted:
        v -= est["overtime"] * terms["unit_price"] * (quoted - lead)
    return v


def price_for_value(case, terms, est, target):
    """The unit price at which `terms` are worth `target` to the supplier (value rises with price)."""
    lo, hi = 0.0, max(1.0, target) * 3
    for _ in range(60):
        mid = (lo + hi) / 2
        if value(case, {**terms, "unit_price": mid}, est) < target:
            lo = mid

    """Every combination of allowed non-price values: [{field: value}]."""
    opts = case.get("term_options") or {}
    fields = [f for f in case["negotiable"] if f != "unit_price" and opts.get(f)]
    return [dict(zip(fields, combo, strict=True)) for combo in itertools.product(*(opts[f] for f in fields))]


# Where a value costs us nothing more, the side the supplier prefers: a later delivery needs no
# overtime, a longer contract and a larger volume give it security (months beyond our horizon
# cost us nothing), a looser defect commitment and a smaller chargeback cost it less.
FRIENDLY = {
    "lead_time_days": 1,
    "contract_months": 1,
    "volume_per_year": 1,
    "ppm_commitment": 1,
    "chargeback_eur_per_complaint": -1,
    "tooling_eur": 1,
}


def friendliness(terms):
    """Higher is better for the supplier."""
    return tuple(FRIENDLY[f] * (terms.get(f) or 0) for f in FRIENDLY if f in terms)


def plan_terms(case, std, est, ref_terms, ref_price):
    """The non-price terms that cost us least once the supplier prices them at its own valuation:
    for every allowed combination, the price worth the same to it as `ref_price` at `ref_terms`,
    then C at that price; among equal C, the supplier's favourite. Returns (terms with that price, C)."""
    target = value(case, {**ref_terms, "unit_price": ref_price}, est)
    rows = []
    for combo in options(case) or [{}]:
        terms = complete_offer(case, {**ref_terms, **combo, "unit_price": ref_price})
        terms["unit_price"] = round(price_for_value(case, terms, est, target), 2)
        if not must_haves_ok(case, terms, std):
            continue
        rows.append((cost(case, terms, std, est), terms))
    if not rows:
        return None
    low = min(c for c, _ in rows)
    ties = [(c, t) for c, t in rows if c <= low + max(1.0, abs(low) * 1e-5)]
    c, terms = max(ties, key=lambda r: friendliness(r[1]))
    return terms, c


def at_price(case, terms, price):
    return {**terms, "unit_price": round(price, 2)}


def relationship_optimum(case, terms, std, est, lo, hi):
    """Relationship goals: the price in [lo, hi] with the lowest C, relationship charge included
    (C falls with price until the margin charge grows faster). Without a full-cost estimate: lo."""
    if case["buyer"].get("category_goal") not in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS or not est.get("full_cost"):
        return None
    best_p, best_c = lo, math.inf
    steps = 200
    for i in range(steps + 1):
        p = lo + (hi - lo) * i / steps
        c = cost(case, at_price(case, terms, p), std, est)
        if c < best_c - 1e-6:
            best_p, best_c = p, c
    return round(best_p, 2)
   1 """The negotiation policy, per supplier thread: plan the non-price terms by C at the supplier's
   2 own valuation, open below its quote, then move toward its counter round by round so it keeps
   3 conceding, with verified claims spread over the rounds. Close on its final offer, its agreement or
   4 the round limit; in relationship goals stop at the price where C is lowest.
   5 
   6 What the suppliers showed (sandbox and practice, `docs/learnings.md`):
   7 - they concede only after a move from us and agree as soon as our sheet reaches the counter they
   8   would make, so our sheet stays below their counter until the end;
   9 - every verified claim they take into account lowers where they stop, most of it in round 1;
  10 - patience runs out at a cumulative gap of about 40 % between our sheets and their counters
  11   (summed per round, relative to their price), much earlier for a supplier selling near its cost
  12   or one that is fully booked: a final offer, or a walk-away;
  13 - a large first concession means a deep floor: then we hold low instead of meeting it."""
  14

  31 # Opening price as a share of its quote at our terms, by category goal. Practice C_best sat 12 to
  32 # 22 % below the quote in leverage, routine and secure-supply cases, 1.5 to 3 % in stabilise ones.
  33 ANCHOR = {"leverage": 0.78, "routine": 0.82, "secure_supply": 0.88, "quality_first": 0.88, "stabilise": 0.92}

  72     def __init__(self, case, pkg=None, complete=None):

  80     # -- setup -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  81     def setup(self, sid, events):
  82         case, s = self.case, Side(sid)
  83         s.std = safe(lambda: standard_terms(events), {}) or {}
  84         sheet_id, quote = standing(events)
  85         s.prof = safe(lambda: profile(self.pkg, sid), profile(None, sid))
  86         self.read_signals(s, latest(events).get("body"))
  87         self.sides[sid] = s
  88         if not sheet_id or quote.get("unit_price") is None:
  89             s.state = "ended"
  90             return s
  91         s.last_sheet = quote
  92         # a bundle's should-cost is unknown: one component's cost is not the price unit of the kit
  93         parts = case.get("parts") or []
  94         full_cost, own_plant = (
  95             safe(lambda: self.full_cost(parts[0], sid), (None, False)) if len(parts) == 1 else (None, False)
  96         )
  97         lead = quote.get("lead_time_days") or s.std.get("lead_time_days")
  98         overtime = 0.005 if "capacity_full" in s.prof["signals"] else 0.001
  99         s.est = eco.estimate(
 100             case, s.std or quote, s.prof["rate"], full_cost, safe(lambda: self.real_ppm(sid)), lead, overtime
 101         )
 102         q_price = quote["unit_price"]
 103         goal, signals = case["buyer"].get("category_goal"), s.prof["signals"]
 104         sustainable = case["buyer"].get("sustainable_margin_pct") or 0
 105         if full_cost and goal in eco.RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
 106             # it quoted with its margin: a should-cost above that is our estimate's error (P02: 374.95
 107             # against a quote of 370.96; the relationship charge of the deals says about 368)
 108             full_cost = min(full_cost, eco.value(case, quote, s.est) * (1 - sustainable / 100))
 109             s.est["full_cost"] = full_cost
 110         ratio = ANCHOR.get(goal, 0.85)
 111         near_cost = bool(own_plant and full_cost >= 0.98 * q_price)  # it sells at our cost estimate
 112         if goal in eco.RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
 113             s.budget = 0.3
 114         if "price_frozen" in signals:
 115             ratio = max(ratio, 0.95)  # its list price does not move far; a deep cut only costs patience
 116         if "capacity_full" in signals:
 117             ratio, s.budget = max(ratio, 0.93), min(s.budget, 0.16)
 118         if near_cost:
 119             ratio, s.budget = max(ratio, 0.97), min(s.budget, 0.14)
 120         current = case["buyer"].get("current_unit_price")
 121         if case.get("type") == "price_increase" and current:
 122             ratio = min(ratio, current / q_price)  # a price increase opens at today's price at most
 123         ratio = max(ANCHOR_MIN, ratio)
 124         # terms planned at the price we open with: coverage pays off at a low price, not at the quote
 125         planned = safe(lambda: eco.plan_terms(case, s.std, s.est, quote, q_price * ratio))
 126         s.terms = planned[0] if planned else eco.complete_offer(case, eco.at_price(case, quote, q_price * ratio))
 127         s.anchor = s.terms["unit_price"]
 128         s.quote = safe(
 129             lambda: round(eco.price_for_value(case, s.terms, s.est, eco.value(case, quote, s.est)), 2), q_price
 130         )
 131         if full_cost and not near_cost:
 132             s.target = safe(lambda: eco.relationship_optimum(case, s.terms, s.std, s.est, full_cost * 0.85, s.quote))
 133         safe(lambda: self.trade_clause(s, quote, full_cost))
 134         s.claims = safe(lambda: self.bank.for_supplier(sid, q_price), [])
 135         self.note(
 136             sid,
 137             "setup",
 138             quote=quote,
 139             std=s.std,
 140             profile=s.prof,
 141             full_cost=full_cost,
 142             near_cost=near_cost,
 143             terms=s.terms,
 144             quote_at_terms=s.quote,
 145             anchor=s.anchor,
 146             target=s.target,
 147             budget=s.budget,
 148             claims=[c["text"] for c in s.claims],
 149         )
 150         return s

 152     def trade_clause(self, s, quote, full_cost):
 153         """An index clause the supplier values more than it costs us (its driver rose over the
 154         year, the case's path is small): offer it from the start at the price worth the same to it
 155         as our anchor without it, and in a relationship goal no lower than the relationship
 156         optimum, where it is agreed at once (P02: Nordmark agreed to a 5 % copper deadband 4 %
 157         below its fixed price). No trade where its value equals our cost (P08, P18)."""
 158         case = self.case
 159         if "index_clause" not in case["negotiable"] or quote.get("index_clause"):
 160             return
 161         for clause in case.get("term_options", {}).get("index_clause") or []:
 162             if clause and clause.get("series") not in s.est["index_moves"]:
 163                 move = self.bank.move12(clause["series"])
 164                 if move is not None:
 165                     s.est["index_moves"][clause["series"]] = move
 166         clause = eco.clause_trade(case, s.est)
 167         if not clause or s.terms.get("index_clause") == clause:
 168             return
 169         target_value = eco.value(case, s.terms, s.est)  # our anchor as it is worth to the supplier
 170         terms = {**s.terms, "index_clause": clause}
 171         price = eco.price_for_value(case, terms, s.est, target_value)
 172         floor = None
 173         if full_cost and case["buyer"].get("category_goal") in eco.RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
 174             floor = eco.relationship_optimum(case, terms, s.std, s.est, full_cost * 0.85, s.quote)
 175             price = max(price, floor or 0.0)
 176         if not eco.must_haves_ok(case, eco.at_price(case, terms, price), s.std):
 177             return
 178         s.terms = eco.at_price(case, terms, price)
 179         s.anchor = s.terms["unit_price"]
 180         s.target = floor or s.target
 181         self.note(s.sid, "clause_trade", clause=clause, anchor=s.anchor, target=s.target)
 182 
 183     def full_cost(self, part, sid):
 184         """(should-cost of the part, whether it models this supplier's own plant): full cost
 185         without margin. A generic estimate (a German cost base) says little about one supplier."""
 186         rows = self.bank.query("SELECT id, supplier_id, unit_cost FROM should_cost WHERE part_id = ?", (part,))
 187         own = [r for r in rows if r.get("supplier_id") == sid]
 188         if own:
 189             return own[0]["unit_cost"], True
 190         generic = [r for r in rows if not r.get("supplier_id")]
 191         if generic:
 192             return generic[0]["unit_cost"], False
 193         for ref in self.bank.ids("cost:"):  # the case's own facts (no table rows)
 194             f = self.bank.fact(ref)
 195             if f and f.get("part") == part and f.get("unit_cost"):
 196                 return f["unit_cost"], f.get("supplier") == sid
 197         return None, False
 198 
 199     def real_ppm(self, sid):
 200         """The defect rate it really delivers (latest scorecard), what a chargeback costs it."""
 201         ids = self.bank.ids(f"sc:{sid.split(':')[-1]}@")
 202         f = self.bank.fact(ids[-1]) if ids else None
 203         return f.get("ppm") if f else None

 205     def restore(self, sid, events):
 206         """A resumed session (a crash, a restart): rebuild what we sent and what it answered from
 207         the thread, so the next move continues the path instead of opening at the anchor again."""
 208         s = self.sides[sid]
 209         ours = [m for m in events if m.get("from") == "buyer" and m.get("term_sheets")]
 210         if s.state == "ended" or not ours:
 211             return
 212         s.terms = eco.complete_offer(self.case, ours[-1]["term_sheets"][0]["terms"])
 213         theirs = None
 214         for m in events:
 215             if m.get("from") == "buyer":
 216                 self.used.update(m.get("refs") or [])
 217                 if m.get("term_sheets"):
 218                     price = self.their_price(s, m["term_sheets"][0]["terms"])
 219                     s.ours.append(price)
 220                     s.gaps.append(max(0.0, (theirs - price) / theirs) if theirs else 0.0)
 221             else:
 222                 sheets = m.get("term_sheets") or []
 223                 if sheets and sheets[0].get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") is not None:
 224                     theirs = self.their_price(s, sheets[0]["terms"])
 225                     if s.ours:
 226                         s.theirs.append(theirs)
 227         if events and events[-1].get("from") != "buyer" and s.theirs:
 228             s.theirs.pop()  # the latest reply is read by move() like any fresh reply
 229         self.note(sid, "restore", ours=s.ours, theirs=s.theirs, terms=s.terms)

 232     def read_signals(self, s, body):
 233         """Persona traits in its own e-mail (a supplier the package does not know, or news since):
 234         merged into the profile; a cash need raises what money now is worth to it."""

 241             if s.est:

 245     def their_price(self, s, terms):
 246         """Its sheet as a price at our planned terms (same value to it)."""
 247         same = all(terms.get(k) == v for k, v in s.terms.items() if k != "unit_price" and k in terms)
 248         if same:
 249             return terms["unit_price"]
 250         v = eco.value(self.case, terms, s.est)
 251         return round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, s.terms, s.est, v), 2)

 253     def switch(self, s, new, why):
 254         """Plan new non-price terms; our last price moves to the same value for the supplier."""
 255         if s.ours:
 256             v = eco.value(self.case, eco.at_price(self.case, s.terms, s.ours[-1]), s.est)
 257             s.ours[-1] = round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, new, s.est, v), 2)
 258         if s.theirs:
 259             v = eco.value(self.case, eco.at_price(self.case, s.terms, s.theirs[-1]), s.est)
 260             s.theirs[-1] = round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, new, s.est, v), 2)
 261         s.terms = {**new}
 262         self.note(s.sid, "switch_terms", why=why, terms={k: v for k, v in new.items() if k != "unit_price"})

 264     def adopt(self, s, sheets):
 265         """Compare complete quoted packages, then switch once to the cheapest useful one."""
 266         if not s.ours:
 267             return
 268         case = self.case
 269         standing = sheets[0]["terms"]
 270         planned_cost = eco.cost(
 271             case, eco.at_price(case, s.terms, self.their_price(s, standing)), s.std, s.est
 272         )
 273         candidates = []
 274         for sheet in sheets:
 275             new = eco.quoted_offer(case, sheet["terms"], s.std)
 276             if new is None or all(new.get(k) == v for k, v in s.terms.items() if k != "unit_price"):
 277                 continue
 278             c = eco.deal_cost(case, new, s.std, s.est)
 279             if c is not None and c < planned_cost - max(1.0, 0.001 * planned_cost):
 280                 candidates.append((c, new))
 281         if candidates:
 282             _, new = min(candidates, key=lambda row: (row[0], repr(sorted(row[1].items()))))
 283             self.switch(s, new, "complete quoted package costs us less")

 285     # -- one move ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 286     def move(self, sid, threads, writer_s=llm.TIMEOUT_S):
 287         """The next message to this supplier: {"message": ...}, or None when the thread is done.
 288         `writer_s`: what the supplier clocks leave for the model paragraph."""
 289         case, s, events = self.case, self.sides[sid], threads[sid]
 290         self.writer_s = writer_s
 291         s.prev_state = s.state
 292         last = latest(events)
 293         status = last.get("status")
 294         if s.state == "ended" or status in ENDED:
 295             s.state = "ended"
 296             return None
 297         sheets = [sh for sh in last.get("term_sheets") or [] if sh.get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") is not None]
 298         if not sheets:
 299             s.state = "ended" if not standing(events)[0] else "done"
 300             return None
 301         s.std = standard_terms(events) or s.std
 302         fresh = s.last_reply is not last
 303         if fresh:
 304             terms_before = dict(s.terms)
 305             self.adopt(s, sheets)
 306             s.term_change = any(sheets[0]["terms"].get(k, v) != v for k, v in terms_before.items() if k != "unit_price")
 307             s.theirs.append(self.their_price(s, sheets[0]["terms"]))
 308             s.last_sheet = sheets[0]["terms"]
 309             s.last_reply = last
 310             s.asks = reader.asks(last.get("body"))
 311             self.read_signals(s, last.get("body"))
 312             if s.target is not None:
 313                 s.target = eco.relationship_optimum(
 314                     case, s.terms, s.std, s.est, s.est["full_cost"] * 0.85,
 315                     max(s.est["full_cost"] * 0.85, s.theirs[-1]),
 316                 )
 317         theirs = s.theirs[-1]
 318         if s.state in ("mirror", "closing"):  # we sent its own sheet or our target: done
 319             s.state = "done"
 320             return None
 321         left = self.moves_left(s, events)
 322         if status in DONE or left <= 0:
 323             return self.finish(s, sheets, events, theirs, left)
 324         if s.target and theirs <= s.target * 1.002:
 325             # relationship goal: below the target a lower price costs more than it saves
 326             s.state = "closing"
 327             return self.send(s, [eco.at_price(case, s.terms, max(s.target, theirs))], [], events, theirs)
 328         if s.ours and theirs <= s.ours[-1]:  # it came below what we offered: take it
 329             return self.finish(s, sheets, events, theirs, left)
 330         price, n_claims = self.next_price(s, theirs)
 331         claims = self.pick(s, n_claims, threads)
 332         return self.send(s, [eco.at_price(case, s.terms, price)], claims, events, theirs)
 333 
 334     def moves_left(self, s, events):
 335         """Messages we may still send: the arena counts a late message as a round too."""
 336         return moves_left(self.case, events) - s.late
 337 
 338     def next_price(self, s, theirs):
 339         """Our next price at s.terms: open at the anchor; then a share of the gap, held low after a
 340         large concession, and within the patience budget."""
 341         if not s.ours:
 342             return s.anchor, FIRST_CLAIMS
 343         last = s.ours[-1]
 344         gap = (theirs - last) / theirs
 345         conceded = (s.theirs[-2] - theirs) / s.theirs[-2] if len(s.theirs) > 1 else 0.0
 346         share = FRACTION
 347         if len(s.ours) == 1 and conceded >= DEEP and not s.term_change:
 348             # a deep floor: a pure price drop this large means it moves fast on its own (job shops,
 349             # P05, D02) and agrees at our sheet next: hold the anchor (Dralveck agreed at a held
 350             # 27.86, at 28.07 after an 8 % step); a drop that came with terms it added (an index
 351             # clause, P08, P18) is not one
 352             share = 0.0
 353         left = max(0.0, s.budget - sum(s.gaps))
 354         new_gap = min(gap * (1 - share), left / 2)
 355         if s.budget < 0.2:  # a touchy supplier: small, steady gaps
 356             new_gap = min(new_gap, 0.015)
 357         price = theirs * (1 - new_gap)
 358         price = max(price, last * (1 + MIN_MOVE))
 359         price = min(price, theirs * 0.998)
 360         return round(max(price, last), 2), LATER_CLAIMS
 361 
 362     def finish(self, s, sheets, events, theirs, left):
 363         """Its final word, its agreement or our last message: if one of its alternatives costs us
 364         less than its standing sheet, send that sheet back so it agrees to it; else done."""
 365         case = self.case
 366         std = s.std
 367         c_stand = eco.deal_cost(case, sheets[0]["terms"], std, s.est)
 368         alts = []
 369         for sh in sheets[1:]:
 370             terms = eco.quoted_offer(case, sh["terms"], std)
 371             c = eco.deal_cost(case, terms, std, s.est) if terms is not None else None
 372             if c is not None:
 373                 alts.append((c, terms))
 374         if alts and left > 0:
 375             c, terms = min(alts, key=lambda row: row[0])
 376             if c_stand is None or c < c_stand - 1.0:
 377                 s.state = "mirror"
 378                 return self.send(s, [terms], [], events, theirs)
 379         s.state = "done"
 380         return None

 382     def pick(self, s, n, threads):
 383         """The next unused claims for this supplier: in an RFQ the cheapest rival offer first (a new
 384         offer is a new argument every round), then its own claims, strongest first."""
 385         out = []
 386         rivals = []
 387         for other, events in threads.items():
 388             if other == s.sid or latest(events).get("status") in ENDED:
 389                 continue
 390             oid, t = standing(events)
 391             if oid and t.get("unit_price") and s.theirs:
 392                 price = self.their_price(s, t)
 393                 if price < s.theirs[-1]:
 394                     rivals.append((price, rival_offer(other, oid, t["unit_price"])))
 395         pool = [c for _, c in sorted(rivals, key=lambda r: r[0])[:1]] + s.claims
 396         for c in pool:
 397             key = [(s.sid, i) if c.get("rival") else i for i in c["ids"]]
 398             if any(k in self.used for k in key):
 399                 continue
 400             out.append(c)
 401             if len(out) >= n:
 402                 break
 403         return out

 405     def facts(self, s, sheets, claims, moved, statements, attachments):
 406         """Plain statements the model may use, true by construction; its asks come first so the

33	    """The non-price terms that cost us least once the supplier prices them at its own valuation:
34	    for every allowed combination, the price worth the same to it as `ref_price` at `ref_terms`,

57	    """Relationship goals: the price in [lo, hi] with the lowest C, relationship charge included

59	    if case["buyer"].get("category_goal") not in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS or not est.get("full_cost"):

def options(case):
    """Every combination of allowed non-price values: [{field: value}]."""
    opts = case.get("term_options") or {}
    fields = [f for f in case["negotiable"] if f != "unit_price" and opts.get(f)]
    return [dict(zip(fields, combo, strict=True)) for combo in itertools.product(*(opts[f] for f in fields))]


# Where a value costs us nothing more, the side the supplier prefers: a later delivery needs no
# overtime, a longer contract and a larger volume give it security (months beyond our horizon
# cost us nothing), a looser defect commitment and a smaller chargeback cost it less.
FRIENDLY = {
    "lead_time_days": 1,
    "contract_months": 1,
    "volume_per_year": 1,
    "ppm_commitment": 1,
    "chargeback_eur_per_complaint": -1,
    "tooling_eur": 1,
}


def friendliness(terms):
    """Higher is better for the supplier."""
    return tuple(FRIENDLY[f] * (terms.get(f) or 0) for f in FRIENDLY if f in terms)


def plan_terms(case, std, est, ref_terms, ref_price):
    """The non-price terms that cost us least once the supplier prices them at its own valuation:
    for every allowed combination, the price worth the same to it as `ref_price` at `ref_terms`,
    then C at that price; among equal C, the supplier's favourite. Returns (terms with that price, C)."""
    target = value(case, {**ref_terms, "unit_price": ref_price}, est)
    rows = []
    for combo in options(case) or [{}]:
        terms = complete_offer(case, {**ref_terms, **combo, "unit_price": ref_price})
        terms["unit_price"] = round(price_for_value(case, terms, est, target), 2)
        if not must_haves_ok(case, terms, std):
            continue
        rows.append((cost(case, terms, std, est), terms))
    if not rows:
        return None
    low = min(c for c, _ in rows)
    ties = [(c, t) for c, t in rows if c <= low + max(1.0, abs(low) * 1e-5)]
    c, terms = max(ties, key=lambda r: friendliness(r[1]))
    return terms, c


def at_price(case, terms, price):
    return {**terms, "unit_price": round(price, 2)}


def relationship_optimum(case, terms, std, est, lo, hi):
    """Relationship goals: the price in [lo, hi] with the lowest C, relationship charge included
    (C falls with price until the margin charge grows faster). Without a full-cost estimate: lo."""
    if case["buyer"].get("category_goal") not in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS or not est.get("full_cost"):
        return None
    best_p, best_c = lo, math.inf
    steps = 200
    for i in range(steps + 1):
        p = lo + (hi - lo) * i / steps
        c = cost(case, at_price(case, terms, p), std, est)
        if c < best_c - 1e-6:
            best_p, best_c = p, c
    return round(best_p, 2)

 154         year, the case's path is small): offer it from the start at the price worth the same to it

 157         below its fixed price). No trade where its value equals our cost (P08, P18)."""
