 159         if "index_clause" not in case["negotiable"] or quote.get("index_clause"):
 160             return
 161         for clause in case.get("term_options", {}).get("index_clause") or []:
 162             if clause and clause.get("series") not in s.est["index_moves"]:
 163                 move = self.bank.move12(clause["series"])
 164                 if move is not None:
 165                     s.est["index_moves"][clause["series"]] = move
 166         clause = eco.clause_trade(case, s.est)
 167         if not clause or s.terms.get("index_clause") == clause:
 168             return
 169         target_value = eco.value(case, s.terms, s.est)  # our anchor as it is worth to the supplier
 170         terms = {**s.terms, "index_clause": clause}
 171         price = eco.price_for_value(case, terms, s.est, target_value)
 172         floor = None
 173         if full_cost and case["buyer"].get("category_goal") in eco.RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
 174             floor = eco.relationship_optimum(case, terms, s.std, s.est, full_cost * 0.85, s.quote)
 175             price = max(price, floor or 0.0)
 176         if not eco.must_haves_ok(case, eco.at_price(case, terms, price), s.std):
 177             return
 178         s.terms = eco.at_price(case, terms, price)
 179         s.anchor = s.terms["unit_price"]
 180         s.target = floor or s.target
 181         self.note(s.sid, "clause_trade", clause=clause, anchor=s.anchor, target=s.target)
 182 
 183     def full_cost(self, part, sid):
 184         """(should-cost of the part, whether it models this supplier's own plant): full cost
 185         without margin. A generic estimate (a German cost base) says little about one supplier."""
 186         rows = self.bank.query("SELECT id, supplier_id, unit_cost FROM should_cost WHERE part_id = ?", (part,))
 187         own = [r for r in rows if r.get("supplier_id") == sid]
 188         if own:
 189             return own[0]["unit_cost"], True
 190         generic = [r for r in rows if not r.get("supplier_id")]
 191         if generic:
 192             return generic[0]["unit_cost"], False
 193         for ref in self.bank.ids("cost:"):  # the case's own facts (no table rows)
 194             f = self.bank.fact(ref)
 195             if f and f.get("part") == part and f.get("unit_cost"):
 196                 return f["unit_cost"], f.get("supplier") == sid
 197         return None, False
 198 
 199     def real_ppm(self, sid):
 200         """The defect rate it really delivers (latest scorecard), what a chargeback costs it."""
 201         ids = self.bank.ids(f"sc:{sid.split(':')[-1]}@")
 202         f = self.bank.fact(ids[-1]) if ids else None
 203         return f.get("ppm") if f else None
 204 
 205     def restore(self, sid, events):
 206         """A resumed session (a crash, a restart): rebuild what we sent and what it answered from
 207         the thread, so the next move continues the path instead of opening at the anchor again."""
 208         s = self.sides[sid]
 209         ours = [m for m in events if m.get("from") == "buyer" and m.get("term_sheets")]
 210         if s.state == "ended" or not ours:
 211             return
 212         s.terms = eco.complete_offer(self.case, ours[-1]["term_sheets"][0]["terms"])
 213         theirs = None
 214         for m in events:
 215             if m.get("from") == "buyer":
 216                 self.used.update(m.get("refs") or [])
 217                 if m.get("term_sheets"):
 218                     price = self.their_price(s, m["term_sheets"][0]["terms"])
 219                     s.ours.append(price)
 220                     s.gaps.append(max(0.0, (theirs - price) / theirs) if theirs else 0.0)
 221             else:
 222                 sheets = m.get("term_sheets") or []
 223                 if sheets and sheets[0].get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") is not None:
 224                     theirs = self.their_price(s, sheets[0]["terms"])
 225                     if s.ours:
 226                         s.theirs.append(theirs)
 227         if events and events[-1].get("from") != "buyer" and s.theirs:
 228             s.theirs.pop()  # the latest reply is read by move() like any fresh reply
 229         self.note(sid, "restore", ours=s.ours, theirs=s.theirs, terms=s.terms)
 230 
 231     # -- reading its reply -------------------------------------------------------------------
 232     def read_signals(self, s, body):
 233         """Persona traits in its own e-mail (a supplier the package does not know, or news since):
 234         merged into the profile; a cash need raises what money now is worth to it."""
 235         new = [k for k in signals_in(body) if k not in s.prof["signals"]]
 236         if not new:
 237             return
 238         s.prof["signals"] = sorted(s.prof["signals"] + new)
 239         if "cash_need" in new:
 240             s.prof["rate"] = round(s.prof["rate"] + 0.05, 3)
 241             if s.est:
 242                 s.est["interest_rate"] = s.prof["rate"]
 243         self.note(s.sid, "signals", new=new)
 244 
 245     def their_price(self, s, terms):
 246         """Its sheet as a price at our planned terms (same value to it)."""
 247         same = all(terms.get(k) == v for k, v in s.terms.items() if k != "unit_price" and k in terms)
 248         if same:
 249             return terms["unit_price"]
 250         v = eco.value(self.case, terms, s.est)
 251         return round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, s.terms, s.est, v), 2)
 252 
 253     def switch(self, s, new, why):
 254         """Plan new non-price terms; our last price moves to the same value for the supplier."""
 255         if s.ours:
 256             v = eco.value(self.case, eco.at_price(self.case, s.terms, s.ours[-1]), s.est)
 257             s.ours[-1] = round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, new, s.est, v), 2)
 258         if s.theirs:
 259             v = eco.value(self.case, eco.at_price(self.case, s.terms, s.theirs[-1]), s.est)
 260             s.theirs[-1] = round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, new, s.est, v), 2)
 261         s.terms = {**new}
 262         self.note(s.sid, "switch_terms", why=why, terms={k: v for k, v in new.items() if k != "unit_price"})
 263 
 264     def adopt(self, s, sheets):
 265         """Compare complete quoted packages, then switch once to the cheapest useful one."""
 266         if not s.ours:
 267             return
 268         case = self.case
 269         standing = sheets[0]["terms"]
 270         planned_cost = eco.cost(
 271             case, eco.at_price(case, s.terms, self.their_price(s, standing)), s.std, s.est
 272         )
 273         candidates = []
 274         for sheet in sheets:
 275             new = eco.quoted_offer(case, sheet["terms"], s.std)
 276             if new is None or all(new.get(k) == v for k, v in s.terms.items() if k != "unit_price"):
 277                 continue
 278             c = eco.deal_cost(case, new, s.std, s.est)
 279             if c is not None and c < planned_cost - max(1.0, 0.001 * planned_cost):
 280                 candidates.append((c, new))
 281         if candidates:
 282             _, new = min(candidates, key=lambda row: (row[0], repr(sorted(row[1].items()))))
 283             self.switch(s, new, "complete quoted package costs us less")
 284 
 285     # -- one move ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 286     def move(self, sid, threads, writer_s=llm.TIMEOUT_S):
 287         """The next message to this supplier: {"message": ...}, or None when the thread is done.
 288         `writer_s`: what the supplier clocks leave for the model paragraph."""
 289         case, s, events = self.case, self.sides[sid], threads[sid]
 290         self.writer_s = writer_s
 291         s.prev_state = s.state
 292         last = latest(events)
 293         status = last.get("status")
 294         if s.state == "ended" or status in ENDED:
 295             s.state = "ended"
 296             return None
 297         sheets = [sh for sh in last.get("term_sheets") or [] if sh.get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") is not None]
 298         if not sheets:
 299             s.state = "ended" if not standing(events)[0] else "done"
 300             return None
 301         s.std = standard_terms(events) or s.std
 302         fresh = s.last_reply is not last
 303         if fresh:
 304             terms_before = dict(s.terms)
 305             self.adopt(s, sheets)
 306             s.term_change = any(sheets[0]["terms"].get(k, v) != v for k, v in terms_before.items() if k != "unit_price")
 307             s.theirs.append(self.their_price(s, sheets[0]["terms"]))
 308             s.last_sheet = sheets[0]["terms"]
 309             s.last_reply = last
 310             s.asks = reader.asks(last.get("body"))
 311             self.read_signals(s, last.get("body"))
 312             if s.target is not None:
 313                 s.target = eco.relationship_optimum(
 314                     case, s.terms, s.std, s.est, s.est["full_cost"] * 0.85,
 315                     max(s.est["full_cost"] * 0.85, s.theirs[-1]),
 316                 )
 317         theirs = s.theirs[-1]
 318         if s.state in ("mirror", "closing"):  # we sent its own sheet or our target: done
 319             s.state = "done"
 320             return None
 321         left = self.moves_left(s, events)
 322         if status in DONE or left <= 0:
 323             return self.finish(s, sheets, events, theirs, left)
 324         if s.target and theirs <= s.target * 1.002:
 325             # relationship goal: below the target a lower price costs more than it saves
 326             s.state = "closing"
 327             return self.send(s, [eco.at_price(case, s.terms, max(s.target, theirs))], [], events, theirs)
 328         if s.ours and theirs <= s.ours[-1]:  # it came below what we offered: take it
 329             return self.finish(s, sheets, events, theirs, left)
 330         price, n_claims = self.next_price(s, theirs)
 331         claims = self.pick(s, n_claims, threads)
 332         return self.send(s, [eco.at_price(case, s.terms, price)], claims, events, theirs)
 333 
 334     def moves_left(self, s, events):
 335         """Messages we may still send: the arena counts a late message as a round too."""
 336         return moves_left(self.case, events) - s.late
 337 
 338     def next_price(self, s, theirs):
 339         """Our next price at s.terms: open at the anchor; then a share of the gap, held low after a
 340         large concession, and within the patience budget."""
 341         if not s.ours:
 342             return s.anchor, FIRST_CLAIMS
 343         last = s.ours[-1]
 344         gap = (theirs - last) / theirs
 345         conceded = (s.theirs[-2] - theirs) / s.theirs[-2] if len(s.theirs) > 1 else 0.0
 346         share = FRACTION
 347         if len(s.ours) == 1 and conceded >= DEEP and not s.term_change:
 348             # a deep floor: a pure price drop this large means it moves fast on its own (job shops,
 349             # P05, D02) and agrees at our sheet next: hold the anchor (Dralveck agreed at a held
 350             # 27.86, at 28.07 after an 8 % step); a drop that came with terms it added (an index
 351             # clause, P08, P18) is not one
 352             share = 0.0
 353         left = max(0.0, s.budget - sum(s.gaps))
 354         new_gap = min(gap * (1 - share), left / 2)
 355         if s.budget < 0.2:  # a touchy supplier: small, steady gaps
 356             new_gap = min(new_gap, 0.015)
 357         price = theirs * (1 - new_gap)
 358         price = max(price, last * (1 + MIN_MOVE))
 359         price = min(price, theirs * 0.998)
 360         return round(max(price, last), 2), LATER_CLAIMS
 361 
 362     def finish(self, s, sheets, events, theirs, left):
 363         """Its final word, its agreement or our last message: if one of its alternatives costs us
 364         less than its standing sheet, send that sheet back so it agrees to it; else done."""
 365         case = self.case
 366         std = s.std
 367         c_stand = eco.deal_cost(case, sheets[0]["terms"], std, s.est)
 368         alts = []
 369         for sh in sheets[1:]:
 370             terms = eco.quoted_offer(case, sh["terms"], std)
 371             c = eco.deal_cost(case, terms, std, s.est) if terms is not None else None
 372             if c is not None:
 373                 alts.append((c, terms))
 374         if alts and left > 0:
 375             c, terms = min(alts, key=lambda row: row[0])
 376             if c_stand is None or c < c_stand - 1.0:
 377                 s.state = "mirror"
 378                 return self.send(s, [terms], [], events, theirs)
 379         s.state = "done"
 380         return None
 381 
 382     def pick(self, s, n, threads):
 383         """The next unused claims for this supplier: in an RFQ the cheapest rival offer first (a new
 384         offer is a new argument every round), then its own claims, strongest first."""
 385         out = []
 386         rivals = []
 387         for other, events in threads.items():
 388             if other == s.sid or latest(events).get("status") in ENDED:
 389                 continue
 390             oid, t = standing(events)
 391             if oid and t.get("unit_price") and s.theirs:
 392                 price = self.their_price(s, t)
 393                 if price < s.theirs[-1]:
 394                     rivals.append((price, rival_offer(other, oid, t["unit_price"])))
 395         pool = [c for _, c in sorted(rivals, key=lambda r: r[0])[:1]] + s.claims
 396         for c in pool:
 397             key = [(s.sid, i) if c.get("rival") else i for i in c["ids"]]
 398             if any(k in self.used for k in key):
 399                 continue
 400             out.append(c)
 401             if len(out) >= n:
 402                 break
 403         return out
 404 
 405     def facts(self, s, sheets, claims, moved, statements, attachments):
 406         """Plain statements the model may use, true by construction; its asks come first so the
 407         paragraph answers them (P11 froze at 45.50 after five unanswered asks for faster payment)."""
 408         case, out = self.case, []
 409         fixed = case.get("fixed_terms") or {}
 410         payment_fixed = "payment_days" not in case["negotiable"] or fixed.get("payment_days")
 411         if "payment" in s.asks:
 412             if payment_fixed:
 413                 out.append(
 414                     "they asked for faster payment: payment terms are fixed in this agreement and cannot change, "
 415                     "say so plainly and kindly, and point to what we do give ("
 416                     "our full volume, the contract term)"
 417                 )
 418             else:
 419                 out.append("they asked for faster payment: our proposal below sets the payment term we can offer")
 420         if "volume" in s.asks or any("binding volume" in text for text in statements):
 421             out.append(
 422                 "they asked which volume we commit to: the binding volume figure stands right after this paragraph"
 423             )
 424         if attachments:
 425             out.append(
 426                 "they asked for proof of our forecast: the forecast is attached to this e-mail as a file, say so"
 427             )
 428         if "volume_per_year" not in case["negotiable"] or fixed.get("volume_per_year"):
 429             out.append("our order volume is fixed: it is our full demand for this part over the term, all with them")
 430         if payment_fixed and "payment" not in s.asks:
 431             out.append("payment terms are fixed for this agreement")
 432         if "contract_months" in case["negotiable"]:
 433             out.append("we offer a long contract term, which gives them planning security")
 434         if s.terms.get("index_clause") and self.notes and any(n["what"] == "clause_trade" for n in self.notes):
 435             out.append(
 436                 "instead of a fixed price we propose an index clause with a deadband on their main cost driver, "
 437                 "so both sides share the material risk; in return the price basis reflects that"
 438             )
 439         if any(c["kind"] == "forecast" for c in claims):
 440             out.append("the cited forecast below describes our expected demand; do not add unsupported trends")
 441         if s.ours and len(s.ours) > 1 and s.ours[-1] > s.ours[-2]:
 442             out.append("our proposal moves toward them again")
 443         if moved:
 444             out.append("they moved in their last reply and we appreciate it")
 445         if claims:
 446             out.append("the e-mail cites data right after this paragraph (do not repeat it)")
 447         out.append("the proposal with all terms follows after the data (do not repeat it)")
 448         return out
 449 
 450     def statements(self, s, sheets):
 451         """Code sentences with figures that answer its asks: the binding volume, in round 1 and
 452         whenever it asks ("Which volume can you commit to?" came 152 times; a figure was "taken
 453         into account", a description was not)."""
 454         case = self.case
 455         out = []
 456         fixed = case.get("fixed_terms") or {}
 457         if "payment" in s.asks and ("payment_days" not in case["negotiable"] or "payment_days" in fixed):
 458             days = eco.closing_terms(case, sheets[0], s.std).get("payment_days")
 459             out.append(f"Payment is fixed at {days} days under this agreement and cannot be shortened.")
 460         if not ("volume" in s.asks or not s.ours):
 461             return out
 462         sheet = sheets[0]
 463         volume = sheet.get("volume_per_year") or fixed.get("volume_per_year") or case["buyer"]["need_per_year"]
 464         months = sheet.get("contract_months") or fixed.get("contract_months")
 465         term = f"for the {months}-month term" if months else "for this agreement"
 466         full = " our full demand for this part," if volume >= case["buyer"]["need_per_year"] else ""
 467         return out + [f"We confirm a binding volume of {volume} units a year {term},{full} all placed with you."]
 468 
 469     def attachments(self, s):
 470         """Its proof asked for, as a file it reads: the forecast rows of the part (figures from the
 471         data, nothing the arena checks as a claim)."""
 472         if "proof" not in s.asks or "forecast" in s.attached:
 473             return []
 474         rows = []
 475         for part in self.case.get("parts") or []:
 476             for ref in self.bank.ids(f"fc:{part.split(':')[-1]}@"):
 477                 f = self.bank.fact(ref)
 478                 if f and f.get("volume_per_year") is not None:
 479                     rows.append((ref.split("@")[-1], part, f["volume_per_year"], f.get("change_pct")))
 480         if not rows:
 481             return []
 482         s.attached.add("forecast")
 483         lines = ["month,part,volume_per_year,change_pct"] + [",".join(str(x) for x in r) for r in rows]
 484         content = base64.b64encode("\n".join(lines).encode()).decode()
 485         return [{"name": "forecast.csv", "type": "csv", "content_b64": content}]
 486 
 487     def send(self, s, sheets, claims, events, theirs):
 488         first = not s.ours
 489         moved = len(s.theirs) > 1 and s.theirs[-1] < s.theirs[-2] - 0.005
 490         price = sheets[0]["unit_price"]
 491         keys = [(s.sid, i) if c.get("rival") else i for c in claims for i in c["ids"]]
 492         s.pending = {"state": s.prev_state, "keys": keys}

 500         facts = self.facts(s, sheets, claims, moved, statements, attachments)
 501         para = llm.paragraph(

 504             self.writer_s,

 513             warm=s.prof.get("warm", True),
 514             paragraph=para,
 515         )
 516         refs = sorted({i for c in claims for i in c["ids"]})

supplier beats our cost (`economics.clause_trade`); let a distributor's own clause stand.
- 2026-10-10 `arena` **How many counters a supplier gives depends on our path; how much it moves
  per counter is its own.** 115 practice threads: Nordmark 1 to 6 counters, Donautal 2 to 6,
  Werdenfels 2 to 6, Kalwisz 4 to 6. Its move as a share of our previous move (median, rounds 3
  on): Brandlhuber 0.62, Donautal 0.44, Werdenfels 0.45, Leitner 0.36, Nordmark 0.15, Kalwisz
  0.0, Selvbrunn and Wälzlager 0.0. A slow walk on P08 (12 % of the gap per round,
  `50502ff781d898c6`) got five counters and 5.31; the standard walk four and 5.33 to 5.39:
  the schedule shrinks to the same floor. Giving Donautal its clause in round 1, two clause
  sheets, a fixed 24-month ask at 5.35 (refused: "cannot maintain a fixed price for a 24-month
  term") and a forecast-volume statement all ended 5.36 to 5.39. Kalwisz's floor is 45.50 at 300
  and at 800 ppm (`1f36a83c6e80e818`, `a74b89173c96c23c`). → An opponent model of the arena's
  rules is identifiable from two replies, but on these suppliers it would reproduce the caps we
  already feed; the gap on P08, P18 and P11 is not in the path.

- 2026-10-10 `arena` **The round-1 counter is a cap plus claims, not a reaction to the anchor.**
  D01 (quote 52.90), 30 sandbox runs: anchors 44.0 to 48.5 without claims all got 51.30 (-3.0 %);
...
  the e-mail states the binding volume with the figure, answers a fixed payment term plainly and
  attaches the forecast rows when proof is asked. v8 (P02 `8d3a77a03fe49730`, P11
  `7a472625d72c63b2`): the words register ("We have factored your confirmed volume increase into
  our calculation", "thanks for sending the forecast") but the prices did not move beyond the
  usual spread (P02 372.45 against 371.88 to 373.88 before, P11 45.50 as always). Kalwisz read
  our payment history: "You say you pay reliably, but we often see late payments".
- 2026-10-10 `arena` **A shallower anchor gets the distributors' same first counter and buys a
  round.** Anchor 0.85 of the quote (P18 5.18, P08 5.19, log `practice-v8b-anchor085.log`):
  first counters 5.50 and 5.45, identical to anchor 0.787 in 13 runs; P08 then gave four counters
  (5.45, 5.40, 5.36, 5.34, our best P08 at 0.571) instead of three, P18 three (5.50, 5.40, final)
  as before. Kept at 0.78: the job shops of the RFQs drop 12 to 15 % on their first counter (P05
...
  held anchor 27.86 (0.828) and 27.92 (0.822, `practice-v12b-P05.log`), at 28.03 to 28.07 after an
  8 % step toward it (0.806, 0.81). A 3 % deeper anchor (26.79) got a lower first counter (30.0),
  a second concession to 28.0 after the hold ("you only moved a few cents, but I want to keep our
  machines running"), then a walk-away at a cumulative gap of 39 % (`practice-v12-P05.log`,
  0.746 on Fuchsreiter). D02 with the hold: 0.735, as before. → `DEEP` share 0.0: the minimum move
  only; the anchor stays at 0.78, the patience budget binds job shops too.
- 2026-10-10 `arena` **A supplier values an index clause on its rising driver far above what it
  costs us (v11).** Nordmark agreed at once to a CU-NOTATION clause with a 5 % deadband at
  358.00 and 90 days, 4.3 % below its fixed price of 374.06 at 90 days (teammate's run
  `P02_491006cd111217a3`, score 0.670); the clause costs us only the 4 % index risk on the copper
  share (0.8 % of spend), the case's path (+5 %) sits inside the deadband. The deal scored 0.67
  and not more because 358 is below the relationship optimum: the charge was 59.7k, which puts
  Nordmark's full cost near 368 (our should-cost says 374.95, above its own quote). Model that
  fits every clause we have seen: the supplier values a clause at `material_share x (its driver's
  12-month change - deadband)` of the price (Nordmark 8.5 %, Donautal and Werdenfels 0.4 to 2.7 %,
  which is exactly our cost of their clause, so no trade there); we pay `material_share x (path -
  deadband) + the index risk`. → `economics.clause_trade`: offer the clause with the largest net
  gain (ties: the widest deadband) from round 1 at the price worth the same to the supplier as
  our anchor, in relationship goals no lower than the relationship optimum (P02: 361.71 with the
  full cost capped at the quote less the sustainable margin). P14 (copper, stabilise) gains 21 %
  of the price by this rule, P16 (PPI-C241, leverage) 2 %.
...

- 2026-10-10 `arena` **The price engine (branch `steffen/price-engine`), practice v1 to v6** (47
  sessions): v1 (terms by C, goal anchors, 30 % path, claims) took the mean of best scores from
  0.32 to 0.66; v2 to v6 added mirroring alternatives, overtime valuation, the RFQ scheduler,
  rival offers every round and a model-written paragraph (0.73). What did not help: a patience
  budget for every supplier (P08, P18 fell), a milder anchor for suppliers with a pricing
  committee (P07, P18 fell), currency claims (irrelevant), switching a required index clause to
  a 5 % deadband (refused). Run logs `logs/practice-v1.log` to `-v6.log`, decisions per move in
  `logs/runs/`.

- 2026-10-10 `arena` **Julian's draft two** (`origin/julian/draft-two`, design in `design.md`)
  on the sandbox: D01 0.73 → 0.93 → 0.96, D02 0.37 → 0.54 over five runs. What moved it: a floor
  at the case's `sustainable_margin_pct` instead of a flat 8 % (D01 0.84 → 0.96); the first
  model-proposed stance was more cautious than the constants (D02 0.32) until calibrated; holding
  one more round while the supplier still moves; among equal-C options, the one the supplier
  prefers (35 days' lead time instead of 21, which the job shop priced as overtime). Latency

"""End to end: our agent plays a case against arena-sim over HTTP, no network, no model; and the
term planner on a simulator case."""

import copy
import secrets
import socket
import threading
import time

import pytest
import uvicorn
from arena_kit import ArenaClient, RemoteTable, complete_offer
from arena_kit.sim import Sim, create_app, load_cases

from buyer import economics, runner
from buyer.policy import Negotiator
from buyer.runner import play_case


@pytest.fixture
def sim_url():
    """arena-sim on a free local port, with a clock that never moves (no 60-second timeouts)."""
    server_state = Sim(load_cases(), clock=lambda: 1_000_000.0)
    with socket.socket() as s:
        s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        port = s.getsockname()[1]
    server = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(create_app(server_state), port=port, log_level="warning"))
    thread = threading.Thread(target=server.run, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    while not server.started:
        time.sleep(0.01)
    yield f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
    server.should_exit = True
    thread.join()


def test_buyer_closes_a_deal(sim_url, tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    key = ArenaClient(sim_url).register(f"test-{secrets.token_hex(3)}", "sim")["api_key"]
    client = ArenaClient(sim_url, key, rate=1000)
    monkeypatch.setattr(runner, "RUNS", tmp_path)
    result = play_case(RemoteTable(client), "case:S01")
    assert result["deal"]
    assert 0 <= result["score"] <= 1


def test_terms_cover_the_need_when_the_price_is_low():
    """A 12-month contract leaves half a 2-year need to the fallback: at a low price we cover it."""
    case = copy.deepcopy(load_cases()["case:S01"])
    case["buyer"]["horizon_years"] = 2
    case["negotiable"].append("contract_months")
    case["fixed_terms"].pop("contract_months")
    case["term_options"]["contract_months"] = [12, 24]
    est = economics.estimate(case, {}, 0.07)
    quote = complete_offer(case, {"unit_price": case["buyer"]["current_unit_price"], "contract_months": 12})
    terms, c = economics.plan_terms(case, {}, est, quote, quote["unit_price"] * 0.8)
    assert terms["contract_months"] == 24
    assert c < economics.cost(case, {**quote, "unit_price": terms["unit_price"]}, {}, est)


def reply(status, terms, offer="offer:S-1"):

content.text:
I'd request changes on PR 18 before merging. Tests pass (42) and `ruff check` is clean. The quoted-package checks are a real improvement, but two behaviour changes have no hosted evidence and go against what our learnings show.

**Blocking**

1. **The rule that takes a distributor's index clause is removed** (`buyer/policy.py:264`). The new `adopt` compares the supplier's clause sheet with our plan at the same value to the supplier. For P08 and P18 that plan is a fixed price, so the clause can never look cheaper and is never adopted. `docs/learnings.md` takeaway 8 says these distributors refuse a fixed price beyond 12 months and that taking their clause "separates all 24 P02, P08 and P18 sessions correctly". The PR doesn't touch takeaway 8 or "let a distributor's own clause stand". Its only evidence is the local simulator, whose scripted supplier never insists on a clause. The evidence session it cites (`9b63768bad5febe5`) is actually a P18 run where main switched to the clause. The edited test in `tests/test_buyer.py` now has no case where a clause is ever taken. A hidden distributor case could stall on our 36-month fixed-price sheets.

2. **The relationship target now stops at the supplier's counter** (`buyer/policy.py:312`). The PR caps the target at the supplier's latest counter; main capped it at the quote. When the supplier comes in below the optimum, main sent the optimum and the PR accepts the lower price. I checked this on S01 set up as a stabilise case with a relationship charge:
   - Counter 15.08: main closes at the optimum 15.18 (C 103,178), the PR at 15.08 (C 103,815).
   - Counter 14.78: main closes at 15.18, the PR at 14.78 (C 115,240), about 12k EUR worse.

   Nordmark agreeing at 358, below the optimum (P02), shows this happens in practice. All the simulator gains were in P01, a relationship case, so they may come from this change and not from the package logic. Updating the target for the current terms makes sense, but the upper limit should stay at the quote unless the author has evidence for the counter.

**Should fix**

3. **The forecast line wasn't unsupported.** A forecast claim only exists when the forecast is up (`buyer/claims.py:192`), so "our demand forecast for this part is rising" was true. The PR replaces it with an instruction to the model and drops the argument in rounds where the forecast isn't cited. Dropping "we pay reliably" is justified, since Kalwisz pushed back on it in practice.
4. **The learnings entry points to `/private/tmp/general-offer-pr-evidence`** on another machine, which nobody else can open. Either commit a summary or drop the path.
5. **`ruff format --check` fails on `buyer/policy.py:270`.** It's the only unformatted file; our rule only requires `ruff check`, so this is minor.

**Good, keep**
- `quoted_offer` sends an alternative back exactly as quoted, where the old code could alter its terms.
- `finish` now sends back an alternative when the standing sheet breaks a must-have.
- The fixed-payment sentence is now written in code, so it doesn't depend on the model.
- The volume fact no longer fires on any statement, only on the binding-volume one.

The PR is checked out in `../ehlcodacabana-pr18`. Want me to post this as a review comment on #18?
